implementation_notes: Scala on the JVM has no managed prefetch intrinsic (same as Java), so the lever is layout: primitive arrays (Array[Double]) and arrays of primitive-specialised collections stream, while Array[BoxedDouble] or a List of boxed values is a pointer chase. Scala's value semantics make the arena-by-index pattern natural (a Vector of a case class of primitives is stored unboxed in an array of primitives). For a pointer-chasing graph traversal, Scala's immutable collections (Vector, Array) give contiguity that the JVM can prefetch internally. As everywhere on the JVM, the prefetching that matters is the JIT's own, driven by a layout that lets it prove the access is hot and regular; a hand-placed hint in Scala is not a normal move.
idiom_name: no managed prefetch; Array[Double] / primitive-specialised collections and Vector for locality
pitfalls: No managed prefetch in Scala/JVM; the JIT's own prefetching responds to a provably-hot, regular layout.
Array[Double] is a primitive array; Array[java.lang.Double] and List[Double] box every element and become a pointer chase.
Vector of a primitive case class stores primitives contiguously (good); Vector of a reference type does not.
A hand-placed prefetch in Scala is not a real option (no intrinsic) - fix the layout instead.
